body:
Hi, thank you for your contribution! Please note that we already have pretty much this exact logic in the codebase, and it should be enough to simply "alias" `DisplayServer::window_move_to_foreground` to `DisplayServer::window_request_attention`.

The reason this never got done is that I never got the time to research that it was the right solution (on sway it "dings" the window), but I can't think of anything else for the time being and, worst case, sounds close enough for the time being.

> Almost the same as request_attention but sets the serial of the activation_token to hint to wayland that it can raise the window

Welp, I missed this, sorry xD

If we really needed to set the serial, we could do the same to request attention, but as it's all in the same client I have a feeling that it might not really matter in the first place. From my understanding, this protocol was mostly meant for inter-process activation and the "self-activation" thing was mostly an edge case.

I am also somewhat worried that some compositors might complain with a present but out-of-date serial, compared to a missing serial. I'll ask on IRC.

I learned the serial thing from how SDL does it.
https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/f170b33f16a640269b23ff95a4075d15e2f9262a/src/video/wayland/SDL_waylandwindow.c#L2631

The jist of it is that the compositor decides how to show the activation. Whether to ding the window or raise it or whatever else and part of the decision is usually if the activation token has enough info to prove that the transfer of focus is "consentual" from both sides.

I tested it on endeavourOS with KDE plasma and it works there but I didn't test it with any other DE

Yea, that's understandable (although I don't think we can look at SDL stuff????)

I tend to be *extremely* cautious when readings specs because in my experience there *will* be some weird implementation doing their own thing (and there are like, 4 or 5 major-ish ones).

From the spec:

> For instance, if a click triggers the launch of a third-party client, the launcher client should send a set_serial request with the serial and seat from the wl_pointer.button event.

That's why I'm somewhat worried about setting the serial, and probably why I didn't add it in the first place last time. In any case it should be assumed that the request can fail, but I guess that's a possibility on X11 also.

In any case (sorry for double-post), I consider attention request and "bring to top" to be basically the same exact thing, and because of this I think that we should have the same logic behind them. I've also just asked on the Wayland IRC channel about this matter in the hopes that other users can give me their info.

As this PR is quite simple already, perhaps we could put that discussion on hold and begin merging a simple "alias" between the two methods?

What about adding it to the signature of request_attention like so?
`void window_request_attention(DisplayServerEnums::WindowID p_window_id, bool attempt_raise = true);`

I made a distinction because `DisplayServer` has two distinct methods `window_request_attention` and `window_move_to_foreground`

> What about adding it to the signature of request_attention like so?

That would change the whole cross-platform API and still break existing code that calls the other method. I assume other platforms (windows?) have more nuanced operations and would benefit from the distinction.

> I made a distinction because the DisplayServer has two distinct methods window_request_attention and window_move_to_foreground

I see, no worries. In my experience, I think that it's fine that they have the same implementation.

Unfortunately with cross-platform APIs there's never a 1:1 mapping to every platform. Some are going to be "emulated", some can't be implemented, some are going to give dummy values and some are going to be duplicated. That's also why we have feature flags for the most important features, so that the user can fallback as gracefully as possible on different platforms.

Wayland especially is quite different and has a lot of such cases, most importantly global positioning.

Also https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-activation-v1
And I checked the license of SDL before-hand just to be sure (even though no code was copied) and it does not strike me as it being a problem.
Sorry for the double post. To clarify: I meant change the signature specifically in `WaylandThread`. That should not change any cross-platform api, as it is only referenced by `DisplayServerWayland`

@skorpnok

> And I checked the license of SDL before-hand just to be sure (even though no code was copied) and it does not strike me as it being a problem.

I always got terrified of looking at stuff xD I guess as long there is credit given in a comment it should be fine even copying, maybe? Take it with a grain of salt.

> Sorry for the double post. To clarify: I meant change the signature specifically in WaylandThread. That should not change any cross-platform api, which is only referenced by DisplayServerWayland

Ohhhh sorry. Yea it could be done but still, but I am unsure whether it would be worth it. Like, would the flag only set the serial? If it's needed (and I'm still discussing that on IRC), it might make sense to slap it in any case.

Out of curiosity, does it work on your compositor without the serial? I can't test easily right now.

> Out of curiosity, does it work on your compositor without the serial? I can't test easily right now.

Without the serial it only dings the window. With the serial it raises it.
I tried just aliasing it first, before going down the rabbithole.

Thanks for testing! Just for reference, what compositor are you using? I also did some research and I came quite empty handed unfortunately.

On IRC, I got an answer from a kwin developer, and they say that there it doesn't matter and, AFAIU, it's better to add a serial in any case.

That said the difference in behavior you're reporting implies that there's some variety and that my interpretation is possible. Personally, I feel like the most "reasonable" one is that if there's a serial the compositor assumes that the request comes from user input, otherwise it doesn't.

Because of this, I'm afraid that I might need to do some testing across most compositors to figure out what's the situation, like with some recent PRs. The old freenode logs and mailing list might also hide some more info on the rationale.

Sorry for the huge discussion, it's all very... ambiguous and exactly why I put this in the backburner xD

> Thanks for testing! Just for reference, what compositor are you using?

I pretty sure I am running KWin, which is interesting given your comment.

If you're interested, here's the context: https://oftc.catirclogs.org/wayland/2026-08-20

Told ya this stuff is messy :P

> <zamundaaa[m]> Speaking for KWin, serial zero isn't treated any differently than any other outdated serial 

The way I would have read this is that it treats not setting it the same as setting an outdated(invalid) serial. Not that it doesn't matter

> The way I would have read this is that it treats not setting it the same as setting an outdated(invalid) serial. Not that it doesn't matter

Yea you're right, that would make more sense. Still, that doesn't seem totally correct, as the window dings. Maybe they meant that it would be ignored but still give some feedback? I really am not sure.

I actually forgot to give a look at the Wayland issue tracker. Looking there I found this: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/work_items/150

These two answers in particular seem to give a bunch of indications, but the ambiguity still "puts me off" a bit. 

By swick:
> Creating tokens without a serial is valid. What a compositor does with an activation request is compositor defined. In general it is good practice to react with a change of focus or other intrusive changes only if the compositor received a valid token.
>
>If you're looking for a definitive answer of what all compositors will do when they receive an activation request with or without a valid token then you will be disappointed. The protocol leaves this open on purpose.

By emersion:
> * If you have an activation token from another source (e.g. environment), it's most likely been created with an input event serial. If the user hasn't switched focus since that input event was triggered, then the compositor is likely to transfer focus to your toplevel when you send the activate request.
> * If you have an activation token from another source which hasn't been created with an input event serial, or the user has switched focus, or depending on the compositor's policy, maybe the activation token is not deemed strong enough to transfer focus. In that case, the compositor is likely to indicate that your toplevel requests attention without focusing it.
> * If you create an activation token without specifying an input event serial, the activation token is unlikely to be strong enough to transfer focus. In that case, the compositor is likely to indicate that your toplevel requests attention without focusing it.
>
> In other words, one way to implement the "weak attention request" is to create a dummy token with no information specified, then send an activate request. But again be aware that the protocol doesn't guarantee anything, it's all compositor policy.

It really seems like there's some implicit "strength" depending on how complete and up-to-date the token is.

Ugh, maybe we should really do a serial/no-serial thing? But what if the operation is *not* born out of input and the serial "sucks"? Maybe that's the expected part??? I guess this is an older or more generic issue (there's also other input-serial based stuff), it just kinda annoys me :(

Given the above, I think we can use your approach, sorry for the huge back and forth!

Implementation wise, I'd keep the single method and have a new 'input' parameter that adds the serial.

Personally I'd also add a chunky comment giving some context on why we don't always add a serial, explaining the whole "strength" concept and linking the relevant issue. I can write it myself if you want. I think I can push to this branch too if you prefer.
Tested, fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/122666
@deralmas Made the discussed changes. Not sure on the name of the parameter though.
Might need to set requesting_surface as well for the other DE's to accept it then. I will add it and test it on KDE. I sadly don't have other linux installs lying around.

requesting_surface is now also set. It still works on KDE. Also, go figure I am using the one DE that seems more permissive than the others.

edit: It works on ubuntu 26.04 LTS as well

Hi, sorry for the delay. I did some testing on a bunch of compositors but got weird results. So I'm not sure what to do.

First of all, and this is unrelated to this PR, it looks like on kwin and mutter the window only ever update the attention status when the window starts to render. This is weird cause the game definitely does not get stuck (I also tried `wl-veil`ing out the fifo global).

Other than that, kwin, mutter and cinnamon treated both methods as a "ding" and nothing else. If my notes are to be trusted (I almost didn't notice it was running on XWayland), Budgie was the only one to raise, and even then it ignored the "less complete" attention calls.

I didn't try all compositor in my ISO cause _both_ kwin and mutter not working as expected is rarely a compositor issue, and they're the major ones.

Because of the above, are you sure you aren't accidentally testing the game under XWayland? I'm genuinely asking cause halfway through testing I was doing the same mistake. It's very counter-intuitive, but the embedded game follows the editor preference, while the standalone game does not (even running the game "without a toolbar" doesn't follow the editor). I uh, never found the time to work on a good UX xD

For reference, I was running kwin 6.7.0 (I didn't check mutter), and ran the following test project:

[window-raise-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32826396/window-raise-test.zip)

It's just two buttons that wait like 5 seconds and do their thing. I would press them and minimize the window. It also prints the current display driver, to avoid testing XWayland once again.

I mainly tested it using the detached script window and clicking the tab again to test if it raises. Since the editor is just another instance of Godot I figured it ought to be representative (this works on both mutter and kwin for me). The sample project you sent doesn't raise on my end either sadly. Mind you, your sample does not raise on windows for me either (but it does ding). Maybe there is some extra caveats with the embedded game (even with it set to floating window)?

Edit: Maybe the delay is causing problems too since the attention mechanism uses the last input event to "prove" that the user intended it.

Oh sorry I had no idea (or forgot if you told me) how you tested the PR, so I just whipped up a random test project.

> Maybe there is some extra caveats with the embedded game (even with it set to floating window)?

As long as it doesn't have the toolbar (which confusingly enough makes it embedded in a floating window)... No, it should be completely standalone. To rule that out I actually also tried "playing" the project, in which case it should completely rule that out.

Your delay explanation makes sense for sure, it's just a bummer that not even attention works... Oh well, if this raises the window shortly after a click that's still an improvement.

I'll test as you described then as soon as I can.

Finally managed to test the thing correctly, sorry for the huge delay!

I can confirm that kwin, mutter, and cosmic work! Unfortunately weston, muffin (cinnamon), jay, and sway do not. muffin and sway pinged while the rest did nothing. They're less important and/or tiling so I think it's not a huge loss, and much more important to see the "major" players being consistent with this.

Overall I think that's a good enough result, given how undocumented this all is. The approach isn't _that_ hacky-feeling either.

Looking at muffin some more, the version (6.6.3) that is packaged with mint 22.3 (recommended version) does not actually have the logging yet. It's very strict requiring exact serial matches per input type and focused surface of the input type but what confuses me is that the code in that version of muffin looks identical to mutter. So why mutter works but muffin does not is beyond me atm. I am also concerned that trying to accomodate muffin might break kwin since kwin does not differentiate between which input type the serial comes from and just wants the latest. If you (or anyone else) has an idea please do share. I'll probably look into it more later though.

Testing muffin (cinnamon) on a fresh mint VM also has another problem... When I set godot to wayland none of the windows have titlebars anymore and are impossible to move or resize.

Oh no worries. AFAIK, especially the version I tested (some old version from Fedora 44) is/was experimental or close to that. It's also perfectly possible that they ported/improved that code from mutter since then.

> Testing muffin (cinnamon) on a fresh mint VM also has another problem... When I set godot to wayland none of the windows have titlebars anymore and are impossible to move or resize.

That's cause you need libdecor installed. Hopefully the log mentioned that but either way it's yet another quite unintuitive thing I should've polished, sometime, somehow :sweat_smile:

Edit: To be clear, the fact that the "big players" work perfectly is the most important part. This is a very ambiguous part of the spec either way. If anything, inconsistencies like these would be a perfect reason to clarify the spec.

I pushed the minor change you suggested. I am also experimenting with pulling the serial & surface selection into its own function which only selects them in pair to account for WM that use separate serials. I still need to test that one on mutter and muffin though. Not sure if that should be part of this PR though, if it fixes muffin as well then maybe ig.
edit: I tested it on muffin and that didn't work either :(
Thanks!
